newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds ease at open on post-election worries.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds ease at open on post-election worries.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened softer in quiet dealings on Wednesday as investors considered the narrow victory by the reigning Liberal Party after Monday's federal election and the possibility of higher U.S. jobs numbers.

"The election has raised more risks in the mind of the market than alleviating concerns," said Lehman Brothers Vice-President Michael Gregory. Investors are debating whether the Liberals may lose their slim majority over the term and if Finance Minister Paul Martin will change portfolios.
Canada's 30-year benchmark slipped C$0.16 to C$112.21, yielding 7.019 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond slipped 10/32 to yield 6.90 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowedly slightly to 12 basis points from 13 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The governing Liberals won 155 of 301 seats in Canada's Parliament, a majority of just four seats.
A trader dismissed concerns that Martin may step down. "It's not concerned to be a big concern."
Gregory added that even if Martin leaves, the Liberal government is well on its way to taming Canada's annual deficit. "They've wrestled the deficit genie; it's back in the bottle."

North American bonds also softened as investors eyed Friday's U.S. employment numbers. "The market is bracing itself for higher-than-expected jobs," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Vice-President Andrew Spence.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.26 to C$105.31 to yield 6.506 percent and the U.S. 10-year slipped 6-32 to 6.64 percent. The negative spread between the two traded flat at 13 basis points from Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.95 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.13 percent.
